newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria moves to end aviation fuel shortage.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria moves to end aviation fuel shortage.

text.p: State-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) said on Wednesday that it had resolved a dispute with the port authority that caused aviation fuel shortage and paralysed flight operations nationwide.

Ports officials stopped handling NNPC's fuel-laden vessels from the southeast and bound to the Lagos area because of a four billion naira ($50 million) debt owed the ports by the oil firm as handling charges, triggering the aviation fuel scarcity.
NNPC said in a statement it had made arrangements to transport aviation fuel to Lagos by road while it had also reached an agreement with the ports authorities on the debt.

Six vessels, including one loaded with 15 metric tonnes of aviation fuel, were expected to arrive Lagos within days from the southeastern oil-producing city of Port Harcourt, the oil corporation said.

The port authority, which is also a federal government agency but which is expected to operate on commercial basis withdrew a credit facility granted NNPC on ports charges to force the oil concern to pay up.
Officials of some airlines said that to sustain flights they had resorted to buying aviation fuel directly from tanker drivers who had cashed on the situation to jerk up prices of jet fuel.
The fuel shortages caused nationwide cancellation of flights on Tuesday. Airport officials said a few flights had operated on Wednesday morning.
